encounters.title: The North Hedge
encounters.summary: Rain has blurred the footprints but preserved their order: one dry crossing joins the unlatched garden door to the school wash yard.
encounters.opening_view: The North Hedge loses its memory one footprint at a time. Wil's kitchen cord stops no neighbor and persuades no dog; rain works at every edge. Shallow impressions soften under newer heels. Pale lime remains in one print, and a dark blue thread catches on the schoolward gate. The lane joins Hearth Hall's garden to the covered school wash yard, but sequence—not destination—is what the mud is about to erase.
encounters.content:
## A path being erased

Wil's kitchen cord has already failed. Neighbors have stepped over it, a dog has gone under it, and rain is rounding every edge. Beneath sharper post-rain heels, a shallower line still runs schoolward. Read what remains by depth and overlap, not by shape alone.

The path leaves Hearth Hall's north garden door, follows a limewashed retaining wall, passes the orchard's low gate, and reaches the school wash yard. Dry, it takes five or six minutes. In the present mud, eight or nine.

## The pre-rain crossing

Under the hedge overhang, shallow shoe impressions lie beneath deep post-rain heels. Their rounded track runs from the map-room lane toward the school without turning to the inn, mill, or green.

Pale Hearth Hall lime sits at the bottom of one old print beneath rain mud. At the low gate, dark blue wool catches on the inner thorn where a schoolward traveler would brush the right cuff. The weave and dye match Orlo's coat; the thread still needs timing and route around it.

The garden door pulls shut by an outer strap but cannot latch from outside. A reconstruction leaves it as Wil found it: apparently closed, latch open, no forced entry.

## The route and the alibi

A traveler leaving at 8:48 can pull the door shut, cross before rain at 8:50, reach the covered wash yard near 8:52, and enter the school by 8:54. Jory's sighting and the pupils' late fourth stanza fit that walk. A school departure at 8:45 cannot support a round trip before rain; testing the route only in current mud overstates the travel time.

The mill fixes the rain. Bram's orchard traces keep him above the lower path. Grain carriers explain older mixed traffic along the broad delivery lane, not the direct pre-rain crossing from the map-room garden.

## What the hedge carries

Lime, thread, timing, door, and Orlo's washed cuff join Hearth Hall to the school. Motive, the blow, and the ghost hearths come from elsewhere.

Tracking magic may distinguish the older crossing, later searchers, and animal traffic. Object-following divination may carry the thread to Orlo's coat or the lime to Hearth Hall. Neither needs to produce a glowing name.

## Keeping the path useful

Wil can close the path, but parents need the school, Cora needs the sluice lane, and Bram's cousins need the orchard gate. Mark the old impressions, sketch their order, lift the thread, and reopen the route. Preserving the sequence matters more than preserving every footprint.

If Orlo flees, his new tracks cut deep and sharp toward the old sheep tunnel. They cannot be mistaken for the earlier crossing.

## Carrying the route into the hall

A measured walk, the door-strap demonstration, the mill's 8:50 mark, the rounded track, and the school evidence placing Orlo at 8:54 make the exhibit. No one need believe that a single blurred footprint is uniquely his.

reference_links.context: The lane's stable joins, gates, turns, and shared use make sequence and measured travel stronger than identity from one mark.
The schoolmaster's routine use of the route cannot establish a particular crossing; timing and physical sequence must do that work.
The constable may mark, measure, and reopen the path so preservation does not become needless closure.
The school wash yard is one ordinary entrance onto the lane, not proof that a particular school user crossed it.

encounters.title: The First-Bell Moot
encounters.summary: At first bell, Bramblewick must decide which joined sequence can bear detention, accusation, and the cost of separating murder from every other village wrong.
encounters.opening_view: The first bell stops, and Hearth Hall answers with silence. Hester removes the reeve's chain before sitting among Amity and three household witnesses. Wil keeps the suspects apart; the schoolchildren remain together near the middle hearth. Merrit's body waits behind the map-room door, and the stopped clock still says nine. Orlo lays his papers in one exact pile. Before the bridge opens, the outside witnesses must say what the evidence can bear.
encounters.content:
## The chain on the table

By dawn the rain has thinned to grey. Hearth Hall is warmer than it was at the killing and less merciful. Benches fill the room. The pupils sit with their families near the middle hearth; six suspects sit apart under Wil Sloe's eye. Merrit's covered body remains beyond the map-room door. The clock still says nine.

Hester lays the reeve's chain on the table rather than around her neck. Amity and three lot-chosen householders sit beside her. Wil keeps the suspects apart; custodians keep their own books. Flood bars the magistrate. Hester recognizes speakers and records the vote, but cannot rule on her accounts or detention. Merrit's invitation seats the outsiders beyond Bramblewick's kin groups without giving them judgment.

The room has one immediate question: what Bramblewick knows well enough to do before the bridge opens. Wil keeps the scene and any detainee. The outsiders may call willing speakers, stage the door and route, recommend a proportionate action, or name Orlo first and build backward. No office supplies forced testimony, a private search, or a verdict. The evidence must carry the action requested.

## Six claims, one sequence

A complete case joins six claims. Orlo listens for whichever one remains loose.

1. **Merrit died before the last bell.** The focused wound, blood beneath rain, and medical interval place death earlier than the stopped clock.
2. **The clock was staged.** Glass fell after blood spread; school chalk wedged the pendulum; the clock had kept good time before supper.
3. **The killer entered lawfully and left north.** No lock was forced; the garden door pulls shut without latching; one pre-rain crossing runs toward the school.
4. **Orlo's school alibi begins too late.** Four stanzas passed without him. His first certain presence is the 8:54 side-door arrival.
5. **Merrit meant to expose a scheme Orlo controlled.** Dead children's names, school warrants, Orlo's hand, seal, key, and register loan join him to the ghost hearths.
6. **Orlo carried the crime from hall to school.** Map-room lime marks his key; the hedge thread matches his cuff; the basin holds blood dilution and Merrit's collar fibers; his account changes behind each discovery.

The acorn weight strengthens the first and sixth claims. It is not required. Nor must Bram's search, Mara's brandy, Cora's grain, Perrin's doses, and Hester's bridge all be resolved before the murder finding.

## Lay the case across the tables

If the players want a sequence, Hester offers one:

- break nine o'clock with body and rain;
- demonstrate the chalk wedge and garden-door strap;
- place the rehearsal sheets beside the mill slate and measured hedge walk;
- show one warrant chain, the burial entries, and Orlo's copyist hand; and
- end with key, cuff, basin, and his successive accounts.

Begin with money, speak Orlo's name immediately, or call him before any other witness. Whatever the order, the final account must carry the whole crossing from map room to school.

## One burden for each witness

Do not repeat every interview. Give each witness narrow work.

**Perrin Moss** identifies the focused blow, harmless dose, and earlier death. If his own alibi remains disputed, the Fen sickroom, used cloths, and measured bottle stand apart from his altered cards.

**Jory Pike** fixes the bell and Orlo's 8:54 arrival. If challenged, Tella's marks, Nibs's rain sketch, the practice candle, and a neighbor who heard only the final stanza remain.

**Tella Reed and Nibs Fen** describe what they did before Orlo arrived. Let their sheets speak first. Amity stops any attempt to make children pronounce upon murder.

**Elsie Sedge** places rain against supper service, sees Orlo moving toward the covered approach, and anchors Mara and Hester in the pantry.

**Cora Bramble** certifies the gauge and emergency stop. Her ergot quarrel may be entered without turning it into the killing.

**Nim Thatch** presents one complete warrant chain from authorization to school redemption. Six years of ledgers need not cover the tables.

**Sister Amity** names the dead children, dates Orlo's register loan, and keeps living beneficiaries out of the burial evidence.

**Bram Alder** demonstrates the garden-door strap and admits his earlier search. His lie becomes chronology when placed before rain and orchard work.

Useful exhibits include separated clock glass, chalk wedge, key register, route measurements, blue thread, frayed cuff, basin sample, certified warrants, and burial copies. Weak custody should burden the affected exhibit, not erase every parallel source.

## Orlo's defense

Orlo takes notes on a pupil's slate. He concedes what he can keep separate.

### Procedure

He asks whether outsiders may accuse a householder, whether a suspect reeve may call the moot, and whether children must testify against their teacher. These are serious objections bent toward self-preservation. Hester's recusal, lot-chosen witnesses, Merrit's invitation, and the pupils' physical records answer them without pretending Bramblewick has become a court.

### Separated facts

He had a key. He uses blue chalk. He controls school warrants. He arrived before the bell. He walks the hedge. He washed at school. Alone, each sentence sounds ordinary. His defense depends on keeping them from becoming a route.

### Alternatives

He assigns the early death to Bram or Cora, the missing leaves to Hester's accounts, blood near school to common injuries, and the thread to ordinary hedge traffic. Each explanation carries one object and drops the rest.

### The children

Once the warrant chain is shown, Orlo stops denying the ghost hearths. The shares bought shoes, meals, medicine, and winter fuel. He asks recipient families to stand so that judgment will look like taking food from the people in front of it. Some stand; others remain seated and weep. Hester reads only the warrant numbers. The village does not need the family names to prove the forged households or the murder.

Orlo forged the rule, kept sole control, killed the man who would transfer relief to another office, and placed the children between himself and judgment. Family names may remain sealed while the warrants, burials, hand, and receiving marks remain public.

### The gap

With an incomplete case, Orlo names the missing link. Motive does not place him in the map room. A route does not prove he walked it. A rehearsal lie does not name a killer. He is right about isolated clues. Convergence is the accusation's strength.

## How much weight the room will carry

### Suspicion

A motive, lie, or unexplained trace supports continued inquiry and record protection. It does not support a public finding.

### Detention

Independent connection plus present risk—flight, tampering, witness access, or an unexplained murder route—supports detention. Wil can hold Orlo while the remaining claim is tested.

### Public accusation

A public accusation should at least explain the earlier death, staged clock or false alibi, school-fund motive, and movement from hall to school. A major gap divides the hall rather than ending the adventure by fiat.

### Complete case

All six claims support a village finding without confession, perfect magic, or the weapon. Anything Orlo says afterward confirms or refuses a case already made.

## When the case is complete

Once every major gap closes, Hester asks three questions: Did Orlo hold the key? Did he arrive only for the final stanza? Were the false warrants in his hand? Preserved records make evasion more damaging than silence.

If exits are watched, Orlo remains seated. He admits the fund and says Merrit meant to destroy it. He may refuse the blow or say Merrit turned toward the cabinet and he struck before deciding to do so. The finding does not depend on either answer.

The householders bind him in the warm store room under rotating guard until the magistrate arrives. Amity and two parents keep the school open. The beneficiary box is sealed, not displayed. Bramblewick secures the murderer without pretending that hungry children were the error.

## When the name is right but the case is thin

A thin accusation divides existing loyalties. Parents defend the teacher who fed their children. Bram's kin demand equal scrutiny. Hester's opponents call the inquiry a diversion from her warrants. Orlo asks to return to school while the village waits.

Answer the actual gap with a preserved clue, one witness, a demonstration, or a smaller demand. Likely results include:

- **detention pending inquiry** after late alibi plus route, tampering, or removal of records;
- **freedom under watch** after motive and lies without physical opportunity; or
- **flight** when detention fails and Orlo knows the hedge, basin, or key will close the case.

The first presentation changes the room. It need not finish it.

## Private confrontation

Orlo will meet privately at the school, chapel, or Hearth Hall under the language of protecting children. Mere suspicion teaches him the case's weakness. Early death, late alibi, financial control, and north route produce a bargain: he surrenders keys, warrants, and himself if living beneficiaries remain sealed.

That term may be accepted without concealing the fraud or murder. Warrant numbers, burial entries, and Orlo's hand prove the scheme. A promise to blame another person or destroy the governing records is different; he will not accept the first and will exploit the second.

Do not let a private confession invent unseen clock, route, or weapon facts. Orlo may admit the fund and confrontation. Unsupported gaps remain unsupported.

## Flight and pursuit

Orlo flees only when detention is near and exits are loose. His path runs through the school wash yard, North Hedge, and old sheep tunnel. From the moot, he uses adult argument as cover and leaves through the map-room garden; he does not threaten pupils or create a theatrical disaster.

Fresh tracks cut deep into wet ground, unlike the rounded pre-rain crossing. Pursuit may end at the sheep tunnel, mill footbridge, or flooded lower meadow. Capture secures him; it does not prove the murder. Escape postpones custody while the moot may still reach a finding and the magistrate later issue pursuit orders.

## A wrong accusation

Let a wrong accusation break against evidence. The innocent suspect yields the hidden truth when silence becomes worse: Bram's search, Mara's ledger, Cora's ergot quarrel, Perrin's cards, or Hester's bridge accounts. Each admission explains a suspicious trace and creates its own civic problem.

Orlo supports caution, asks that the accused be watched rather than harmed, and uses delay to move the beneficiary box or prepare flight. Compare the innocent explanation with the clock, north route, and late arrival to reopen the case.

Knowingly accusing an innocent person to protect Orlo is concealment, not failed detection. Later consequences should treat it as such.

## Collateral findings

After the murder finding, Hester asks what else belongs in the morning record.

- **Bram:** unlawful search and debt; inheritance waits for magistrate review.
- **Mara:** duties, closure of the drain route, or a postponed brandy charge; her pantry alibi stands.
- **Cora:** inspection and restitution for contaminated grain; public handling may save the mill from rumor.
- **Perrin:** supervision or removal for altered doses; his wound analysis remains valid.
- **Hester:** resignation, confidence vote, or formal accounting after unauthorized bridge work.
- **Beneficiary families:** private audit, forgiveness of received aid, and replacement of the ghost hearths with a lawful school share.

The morning record may reveal or seal these matters separately. Family privacy does not hide the warrant scheme. A suspect's unrelated offense does not change the murder.

## What Bramblewick keeps

Orlo is identified through converging evidence, secured without harm to the pupils, and delivered to lawful authority. The records survive. Bramblewick keeps the obligation to feed poor children and loses the pretense that one schoolmaster may own the rule because he used stolen money well.

The outside witnesses may leave before every village quarrel ends. The whodunnit is complete when the record can say who killed Merrit, when and how he did it, why he staged the clock, how he reached the school, and why the last-bell alibi is false.

His signed invitation supplies the outside witnesses' standing; his death and plans do not give them authority to decide alone.

His school office remains institutionally real while the moot tests an accusation and protects the pupils.
The school remains a civic institution whose pupils, records, and continuity require protection distinct from any officeholder.
She calls and orders the moot under storm custom while recusing from her own accounts and leaving the finding to witnessed process.
He keeps custody of the scene and any detained person, enforcing the result without becoming the finder of guilt.
She witnesses the proceeding, certifies burial evidence, protects children, and keeps living beneficiary names from becoming spectacle.
The chapel can certify narrow memorial facts while keeping living families and pastoral confidence outside needless exposure.
He presents a bounded warrant chain and its custody rather than covering the tables with six years of private records.
A numbered warrant chain can be presented without opening every sealed bundle or publishing every private name.
The household heir may answer for estate access and orchard work without inheritance expectation becoming a verdict.

A route demonstration may establish distance and possibility while shared use prevents the lane from naming a traveler alone.

revelations.title: Merrit's private archive contains the audit's working papers
revelations.description: Merrit kept earlier Hearth Books, suspect files, wills, and the preparatory comparison for the ghost-hearth audit at his burrow.

revelations.title: The Copper Kettle can reconstruct supper service
revelations.description: Mara's staff controlled food, passages, lamps, and the school tray during the critical half hour, making the inn a timeline encounter rather than merely Mara's workplace.

revelations.title: Moss Apothecary can test the medicine and wound
revelations.description: Perrin's materials and records can distinguish Merrit's accustomed tincture from the focused injury that killed him.

revelations.title: Bram's storm work can be reconstructed in the orchard
revelations.description: The damaged brace, tools, dog, chimes, and rain preserve a physical account of Bram's movements.

revelations.title: Bramble Mill preserves an independent rain clock
revelations.description: The wheel, stream rise, quarter chime, and work notes can fix the onset of rain and explain Cora's scene trace.

revelations.title: The Common Chest contains the disputed disbursements
revelations.description: Payment warrants can separate Hester's bridge expenditure from the fictitious hearth shares and trace redemptions toward the school.

revelations.title: The chapel register can identify the ghost-hearth names
revelations.description: Burial entries can establish that the three household names belonged to children who died before becoming adult hearth-holders.

revelations.title: The school is central to both the money and Orlo’s alibi
revelations.description: Rehearsal records, pupils, copyist tools, warrants, chalk, and the wash yard make the school independently relevant.

revelations.title: The North Hedge can reconstruct the pre-rain route
revelations.description: The low gate and hedge path connect the map-room garden to the school side of the green and preserve traces from before the storm.

revelations.title: The First-Bell Moot will hear the party’s case
revelations.description: Hester has scheduled a public first-bell hearing at which the party may seek detention, name a killer, and present its reconstruction before the circuit magistrate arrives.

revelations.title: Merrit was killed by a deliberate blow
revelations.description: A compact impact behind the left ear killed Merrit; heart failure, poison, and an accidental fall against the clock do not explain the injury.

revelations.title: Merrit died before the last bell
revelations.description: Blood, rain, body changes, and the supper sequence place death around 8:44, before the 8:50 rain and well before the nine o'clock bell.

revelations.title: The tallcase clock was deliberately staged
revelations.description: Its hands were moved to nine, its pendulum was wedged with blue chalk, and its lower glass was cracked after blood had begun spreading.

revelations.title: The killer entered lawfully and left by the north route
revelations.description: An authorized key opened the hall door, and the killer left through the garden and crossed the hedge toward the school before the rain.

revelations.title: A brass acorn map weight was the weapon
revelations.description: One weight's crescent casting flaw matches the wound, and wiping did not remove all blood and green collar fiber from its engraved seam.

revelations.title: Three dead children's names became fictitious hearths
revelations.description: The three impossible households were deliberately copied from children who died before they could hold adult village shares.

revelations.title: The ghost-hearth shares flowed through Orlo's school fund
revelations.description: Coin, grain, food, clothing, slate, and lamp oil were redeemed through school warrants under Orlo's control.

revelations.title: Orlo's public alibi begins only after the murder
revelations.description: The pupils rehearsed without Orlo until the final stanza; witnesses place him at the school near nine but not during the earlier murder interval.

revelations.title: Orlo had the access and materials used to stage the scene
revelations.description: Orlo held a copyist's key, carried blue chalk, knew the clock and records, and could use the hedge route between hall and school.

revelations.title: Orlo Vane killed Merrit Alder
revelations.description: Motive, early death, staged clock, lawful entry, north route, false alibi, and physical linkage converge on Orlo rather than any innocent suspect.

revelations.title: Bram searched Merrit’s papers earlier but worked in the orchard during the murder
revelations.description: Bram's ash and cuff thread come from an earlier intrusion; storm work, tools, dog traces, chimes, and rain account for the murder interval.

revelations.title: Mara paid for silence about brandy and was in the pantry during the murder
revelations.description: Mara's envelopes conceal untaxed brandy, while the burst crock and multiple witnesses place her away from the map room during the killing.

revelations.title: Cora confronted Merrit before supper and stopped the mill during the murder
revelations.description: Flour and Merrit's wrist abrasion come from Cora's earlier ergot dispute; the rising stream and mill work account for her later location.

revelations.title: Perrin altered dosage records, but the medicine did not kill Merrit
revelations.description: Perrin concealed prior overprescription and misstated the cause of death; the bottle contains a nonlethal customary dose, and he treated a feverish child during the murder.

revelations.title: Hester spent common money on the bridge and served pie during the murder
revelations.description: Hester's unapproved payments are physically accounted for at the bridge, while service witnesses place her in Hearth Hall during the killing.

revelations.title: The evidence supports a coherent first-bell accusation
revelations.description: At least three case-bearing conclusions—early death, staged clock, school-fund motive, and Orlo's late alibi—have been established strongly enough to present a named reconstruction.

clues.title: The focused wound behind the ear
clues.description: Merrit's skull bears a compact depression behind the left ear. Its shape is inconsistent with a broad accidental strike against the clock case.
clues.discovery: Automatic on a careful body examination; medical expertise supplies the fracture detail.

clues.title: Rain lies on blood already spread
clues.description: Fine droplets from the open north window sit on top of the blood at the rug edge. The bleeding preceded the rain that began at 8:50.
clues.discovery: Automatic when the blood edge and open window are inspected before the room is cleaned.

clues.title: Clock glass rests on the blood
clues.description: Several lower-pane shards lie on top of the blood pool, while others landed on bare floor. The pane broke after Merrit was already bleeding.
clues.discovery: Automatic when the party records shard positions rather than sweeping the floor.

clues.title: Blue chalk stops the pendulum
clues.description: The clockwork is intact. A snapped blue slate-chalk stub has been pushed between pendulum and case to stop it at the chosen display.
clues.discovery: Found by opening or looking beneath the lower clock case; no clockmaking check is needed to see the wedge.

clues.title: No forced entry and an unlatched garden door
clues.description: The screened clerk's-passage lock is undamaged and accepts authorized keys. The north garden door could be pulled closed from outside but not latched after departure.
clues.discovery: Automatic from preserving both doors and testing their ordinary operation.

clues.title: Residue remains in the nicked acorn weight
clues.description: One brass weight has a crescent flaw and looks freshly wiped. Dark residue and a strand of green collar fiber remain deep in the engraved seam.
clues.discovery: Search of the map table; magnification or forensic skill identifies the residue more quickly but is not required.

clues.title: The authorized key register names Orlo
clues.description: A hook list inside the folio cabinet records keys held by Merrit, Hester, Bram as household heir, and Orlo as authorized clean-copyist. Orlo knew the screened clerk's passage and could reach the map room without force or crossing the public hall.
clues.discovery: Automatic when the party inventories access rather than assuming the locked hall door excluded everyone.

clues.title: Merrit expected the old folios to speak for him
clues.description: Merrit's pocket memorandum says, 'If the clean folio is challenged, fetch years 26–33 from home.' His private archive contains the working comparison.
clues.discovery: Found with Merrit’s effects or disclosed by Hester when she inventories them.

clues.title: The service card fixes the pantry witnesses
clues.description: A supper service card names Mara, Elsie, and the pantry runners for each course. The last entries cover Merrit's departure, the broken crock, and the school tray.
clues.discovery: Automatic in the kitchen papers once the party asks who controlled movements during supper.

clues.title: Perrin's seal marks the open bottle
clues.description: The dark bottle bears Perrin Moss's seal and a measured spoon sits beside it. Its contents and missing volume can be tested at his shop.
clues.discovery: Automatic at the desk; attempting to seize it before recording the seal lets Perrin argue about custody, not erase the lead.

clues.title: Fine flour links an earlier visitor to the mill
clues.description: Fine mill flour lies on the sill and chair, separate from supper meal. Cora admits the dust could be hers and the mill can establish when she left it.
clues.discovery: Automatic observation; distinguishing it from pantry meal is easier after comparing samples.

clues.title: Bram's own story makes the orchard testable
clues.description: Bram says he left the public quarrel to cut loose a storm-damaged brace. His wet knife sheath, dog lead, and claimed work site can preserve or contradict that account.
clues.discovery: Obtained in Bram’s initial statement; Hester and two diners confirm he announced the orchard destination.

clues.title: The audit folio cites Common Chest warrants
clues.description: The three crossed-out chimney entries are paired with warrant numbers held in the Common Chest. Merrit treated those payments separately from Hester’s bridge file.
clues.discovery: Automatic from the open audit folio; exact warrant numbers require taking a clean copy.

clues.title: Hester schedules a first-bell hearing
clues.description: Hester formally asks the party to present whatever case it can support at first bell, before the circuit magistrate is expected to arrive.
clues.discovery: Declared publicly when temporary investigative authority is granted.

clues.title: Merrit traced six years of warrants
clues.description: The audit table lists six years of grain and coin warrant numbers beside the three impossible hearths, all redeemable against records in the Common Chest.
clues.discovery: Automatic on the central audit table.

clues.title: Burial dates sit beside the false hearths
clues.description: Merrit wrote burial dates and 'Open Door' beside all three names. The chapel register can establish who they were and whether they ever qualified as hearth-holders.
clues.discovery: Automatic on the working sheet; recognizing Open Door as the chapel requires only village orientation.

clues.title: School initials recur beside the disbursements
clues.description: Merrit's comparison circles the same receiving initials on meal, shoe, slate, and lamp-oil warrants. A note identifies them as Orlo's school-distribution marks.
clues.discovery: Found by comparing the audit columns or asking Bram how Merrit abbreviated village offices.

clues.title: The clock had recently kept reliable time
clues.description: A clockwright's receipt says the Hearth Hall clock was cleaned, balanced, and tested through all quarter chimes three weeks ago. Merrit recorded negligible drift afterward.
clues.discovery: Automatic in the Hearth Hall maintenance packet.

clues.title: A sketch records the weight’s crescent flaw
clues.description: An inventory sketch of the brass acorn set marks a crescent casting defect on the weight nearest the folio cabinet, matching the asymmetry in the wound.
clues.discovery: Found in the map-room furnishings file; the wound comparison may be made here or later.

clues.title: The wills explain Bram’s earlier search
clues.description: Contradictory wills give Bram a strong inheritance motive. A green-brown cuff thread on the archive drawer and disturbed dust prove he searched Merrit's papers before the murder.
clues.discovery: Automatic if the party inventories the will drawer and compares Bram’s torn cuff.

clues.title: Merrit's index decodes Mara's envelopes
clues.description: Coin envelopes filed as 'Kettle smoke' are wrapped in plum-sugar and imported-yeast slips. A drainage map identifies Mara's untaxed brandy route and explains the payments.
clues.discovery: Search of Mara’s indexed packet; no persuasion is needed once the file is lawfully opened.

clues.title: Older cards expose Perrin’s altered doses
clues.description: Preserved treatment cards show larger sleeping-tincture doses than Perrin's current records. Merrit had evidence of alteration, not evidence that the final measured spoon was lethal.
clues.discovery: Automatic in Perrin’s medical packet; interpretation is confirmed at the apothecary.

clues.title: The three hearth ages are impossible
clues.description: Merrit aligned the three hearth entries with birth and burial dates. Each supposed adult household begins after its namesake died as a child.
clues.discovery: Automatic from the completed portion of the audit comparison.

clues.title: Merrit linked Orlo to the old register request
clues.description: A note from Hester's earlier meeting records Merrit's question: why did Orlo request the burial register six years ago, just before the false names entered the clean folio?
clues.discovery: Found in Merrit’s meeting notes; Hester confirms the question but not its answer.

clues.title: The orchard key opens Merrit’s rear archive
clues.description: A tag on the archive’s spare-key hook says the duplicate is kept in the orchard tool shed for Bram’s estate work.
clues.discovery: Automatic when the party checks who else could enter the burrow; primarily useful if it reached the burrow without Bram.

clues.title: Elsie crossed the green when the rain began
clues.description: Elsie carried a replacement tray across the uncovered green at 8:50 when rain began abruptly. Blood at the open map-room window had already spread before those drops entered.
clues.discovery: Interview with Elsie after she describes the broken crock; her wet tray cloth and Jory’s account corroborate the time.

clues.title: Orlo left the school side before rehearsal
clues.description: Elsie saw Orlo pass behind the pantry at about 8:33 after telling Tella and Nibs to begin without him. His claim of continuous rehearsal presence cannot start there.
clues.discovery: Interview; Elsie fixes the moment by Hester beginning the founders’ reading and the first pie still being uncut.

clues.title: The burst crock fixes Mara in the pantry
clues.description: A split crock, burned cloths, meal spread over compote, and three participants place Mara in the long pantry through the murder interval and onset of rain.
clues.discovery: Automatic inspection plus separate accounts from Elsie, Pip, and Hester.

clues.title: Merrit's burned demand names the old drain
clues.description: A fragment behind the range preserves 'third cask,' 'old drain,' and 'same silence as before.' It confirms extortion over untaxed brandy rather than a poisoning arrangement.
clues.discovery: Search of the kitchen range after Mara admits burning a note or investigators notice fresh ash.

clues.title: Orlo told the pupils to begin without him
clues.description: A note beneath the school tray tells Tella and Nibs to start the Founders' verse if Orlo is delayed and wait for his red-pencil corrections.
clues.discovery: Automatic when the undelivered school tray is inventoried.

clues.title: School meal warrants carry the recurring initials
clues.description: Mara's kitchen book charges enlarged school trays to warrants bearing the same three initials circled in Merrit's audit. The meals reached real children through Orlo’s program.
clues.discovery: Compare the kitchen book with Merrit’s copied warrant initials or later Common Chest records.

clues.title: The service passage confirms a screened north route
clues.description: The covered service way reaches both the screened clerk's passage and a lane to the low north gate and school wash yard. A keyholder could approach the map room unseen, and a pre-rain traveler leaving by the garden could avoid the public green.
clues.discovery: Automatic when Elsie walks the party through service movements.

clues.title: Three diners saw Bram take the orchard tools
clues.description: Bram left the public quarrel carrying a pruning knife and brace hook toward the orchard. The work site can test whether he stayed there.
clues.discovery: Statements from Mara, Pip, or a diner; no one claims continuous observation.

clues.title: Mara saw Perrin measure one spoon
clues.description: Mara watched Perrin pour exactly one spoon from the sealed bottle at 8:17. His shop can test whether that amount could cause the death he described.
clues.discovery: Interview; the measuring spoon remains at the scene as a physical cross-check.

clues.title: Hester joined the pantry work after the reading
clues.description: Hester finished the founders’ reading, carried pie, and helped contain the burst crock through the murder interval. Her financial concealment does not create an unexplained absence.
clues.discovery: Separate accounts from Elsie and Pip plus compote and meal on Hester’s serving apron.

clues.title: Mara delivered old account packets to Merrit’s burrow
clues.description: Mara says Merrit demanded that private payments be delivered to his rear archive, where he kept older account packets and leverage files.
clues.discovery: Obtained when asked where Merrit stored the envelopes; the answer does not require Mara to admit what they purchased.

clues.title: The fracture cannot come from the clock case
clues.description: Perrin or another trained healer identifies a compact impact with radiating fracture, not the broad bruising of an accidental fall.
clues.discovery: Medical examination; a failed check yields the broader conclusion of deliberate blunt trauma without exact geometry.

clues.title: The body had been dead longer than six minutes
clues.description: Cooling, settled blood, and early rigidity are incompatible with death at nine and discovery at 9:06. The defensible interval begins before the rain.
clues.discovery: Automatic to a trained examiner; others can establish “well before nine” with Perrin supervised.

clues.title: One customary spoon cannot explain the death
clues.description: The bottle's remaining volume and recipe show Merrit took one customary spoon. It may cause drowsiness but not the focused wound or immediate death.
clues.discovery: Measure the bottle and compare it with the recipe card.

clues.title: Perrin erased older dosage figures
clues.description: Oblique light reveals erased three-spoon entries beneath current one-spoon figures. Perrin altered records after earlier overprescription.
clues.discovery: Search of the treatment ledger; Perrin admits the change when shown Merrit’s preserved cards.

clues.title: The Fen sickroom preserves Perrin’s interval
clues.description: Cooling cloths, sand-timer doses, missing shop equipment, and the Fen family place Perrin at Lottie’s bedside during the murder.
clues.discovery: Visit or interview the Fen household; no single family statement is the entire support.

clues.title: The wound matches the crescent casting flaw
clues.description: A wax impression or measurement shows the wound’s asymmetric edge corresponds to the nicked brass acorn weight.
clues.discovery: Comparison by a healer, smith, or careful investigator; exact identification is optional to solving the case.

clues.title: Brace cuts were exposed before the rain
clues.description: Fresh cuts, compressed dry sawdust, and rain only on exposed surfaces show Bram freed the storm-loaded cable immediately before 8:50.
clues.discovery: Automatic inspection of the damaged brace before later work disturbs it.

clues.title: Dog and boot traces remain around the work site
clues.description: Nutmeg’s chain wrapped around the post while Bram moved between cuts. Bram’s boots circle the brace and do not form a murder-interval route to the hall.
clues.discovery: Track inspection; rain softens detail but not the tether pattern or general movement.

clues.title: Bram’s cuff and tobacco re-date the scene traces
clues.description: Bram admits searching Merrit’s papers at 6:10 when confronted with matching cuff thread and sweetgrass ash. His traces are real and earlier than the killing.
clues.discovery: Confrontation after comparing his cuff and pipe with the map-room evidence.

clues.title: The mill quarter chime anchors Bram’s last cuts
clues.description: Bram heard the mill’s quarter chime while cutting the final loaded section. Mill operation and stream records can test that point independently.
clues.discovery: Interview at the work site, where the sound carries clearly across the stream.

clues.title: Pre-rain tracks continue toward the low gate
clues.description: Shallow impressions near the lower orchard path have edges rounded by rain, unlike later searchers’ sharp mud prints. They continue toward the North Hedge.
clues.discovery: Automatic route survey; identifying a wearer is deferred to the focused hedge scene.

clues.title: The dry hedge route reaches the school in six minutes
clues.description: Walking from the map-room garden past the orchard’s lower edge to the school wash yard takes five to six minutes on dry ground, matching an 8:48 departure and 8:54 arrival.
clues.discovery: Reconstruction walk; current mud is slower, and the difference itself supports a pre-rain crossing.

clues.title: The orchard shed holds Merrit’s archive key
clues.description: A tagged spare key in the tool shed opens Merrit’s rear archive, where Bram handled estate papers and Merrit kept working folios.
clues.discovery: Automatic when the shed is inventoried or Bram is asked how he entered the burrow.

clues.title: The north window remained open when rain began
clues.description: From the upper terrace Bram saw the lit north casement take the first rain at 8:50. The window was not opened only after the body was found.
clues.discovery: Interview checked against the orchard sightline; this supports the rain sequence rather than Bram’s entire alibi.

clues.title: Merrit mapped Mara’s private delivery route
clues.description: Merrit's extortion packet includes a sketch of the Copper Kettle's old drainage tunnel and notes that Mara's envelopes were delivered through the long pantry.
clues.discovery: Found in the indexed “Kettle smoke” packet even if the party leaves the unrelated casks sealed.

clues.title: Perrin names the inn as the dose witness
clues.description: Perrin says Mara and her service staff saw him measure Merrit's only supper dose. Their work sequence can test both the amount and the timing.
clues.discovery: Obtained when Perrin is asked who observed the 8:17 treatment.

clues.title: Merrit kept Perrin’s shop cards by address
clues.description: The preserved treatment packet names Moss Apothecary and identifies the shop ledger, recipe card, and remaining stock as the controls for the bottle at the scene.
clues.discovery: Automatic in Perrin’s indexed file; this is a lead to the shop rather than proof of malpractice.

clues.title: Cora’s sealed memorandum records the earlier confrontation
clues.description: Cora's sealed notice says she confronted Merrit before supper, asked him to delay public action, and intended to stop Bramble Mill while she isolated the suspect lot and compared the stream log.
clues.discovery: Automatic in Cora’s packet; opening the seal reveals the subject but not whether Cora later followed through.

clues.title: Mara’s kitchen book ties school meals to redeemed warrants
clues.description: Each school meal entry cites a warrant number and redemption date. Mara explains that the originals are surrendered to the Common Chest after payment.
clues.discovery: Automatic when the kitchen book is compared with the enlarged school trays.

clues.title: The audit margin cites the Open Door register
clues.description: Beside the three impossible hearths, Merrit wrote 'birth and burial: Open Door' and marked the chapel register as the independent source for their ages.
clues.discovery: Automatic from the audit folio once the party reads beyond the crossed-out chimneys.

clues.title: The supper ribbons preserve the three children’s names
clues.description: Three faded child memorial ribbons hang among the Founders' decorations. Mara says Sister Amity copied their names from the chapel register and can explain why they never became household entries.
clues.discovery: Noticed among the decorations or disclosed when the party asks whether anyone remembers the three names.

clues.title: Orlo’s stated alibi makes the school a witness scene
clues.description: Orlo bases his innocence on leading the school recitation. The pupils, practice sheets, side entrance, and wash yard can define when that alibi actually begins.
clues.discovery: Automatic from Orlo’s first statement; no suspicion beyond testing an alibi is required.

clues.title: The garden exit opens toward the North Hedge
clues.description: The unlatched garden door opens onto a narrow lane screened from the green. Hester identifies the low hedge gate as the direct route toward the school.
clues.discovery: Automatic exterior inspection after the garden door is recorded.

clues.title: Cora left an ergot sample for comparison
clues.description: A sealed grain sample from Cora waits beside Perrin's reference jars. Her note says the affected lot and stream log remain at Bramble Mill.
clues.discovery: Automatic when investigators ask whether Perrin treated or tested anything connected with Cora’s earlier visit.

clues.title: Perrin supplied the school wash yard
clues.description: Perrin's delivery book lists lavender soap, bandage cloth, and a covered wash basin supplied to Bramblewick School. The school is the proper place to compare Orlo's claimed rehearsal and washing facilities.
clues.discovery: Automatic in the current delivery ledger; the soap becomes incriminating only when combined with route and basin evidence.

clues.title: Merrit drafted the first-bell audit agenda
clues.description: Merrit's prepared agenda reserves the first-bell moot for the audit, names the party as outside witnesses, and lists the order in which the Hearth Book and Common Chest would be opened.
clues.discovery: Automatic among the audit papers; the murder changes the subject but not the scheduled hearing.

clues.title: Merrit planned to take the school fund from Orlo's control
clues.description: Merrit's first-bell agenda rejects a sealed correction, calls for recovery of the remaining ghost-hearth shares, and would place future school relief under the Hearth Book keeper. Orlo faced immediate public exposure and loss of the authority he had assumed over the fund.
clues.discovery: Automatic on the archive table once investigators compare Merrit's intended remedy with the school-fund warrant chain.

clues.title: The inn notice board carries Hester’s summons
clues.description: Hester's signed notice on the inn board orders all six suspects and relevant record keepers to attend a first-bell hearing in Hearth Hall.
clues.discovery: Publicly visible once the reeve posts it after the body is found.

clues.title: Merrit’s wrist abrasion predates supper
clues.description: A shallow cord scrape on Merrit’s wrist is dry and partly closed beneath his supper cuff. Flour is embedded at its edge, placing Cora’s struggle hours before the head wound.
clues.discovery: Careful body inspection; Perrin can estimate the age, but the dried abrasion is visible without him.

clues.title: Merrit walked steadily after the tincture
clues.description: Mara, Elsie, and Pip separately saw Merrit carry the folio to the map room after his measured dose. He was alert, coordinated, and bore no head injury, excluding a collapse already underway.
clues.discovery: Compare the three service accounts; exact minute differs, but all place the focused injury after Merrit left the tables.

clues.title: The wrist scrape is several hours older than death
clues.description: Perrin distinguishes the dry, inflamed wrist abrasion from the fresh fatal trauma. Its embedded flour and age fit Cora’s 5:40 struggle, not the murder interval.
clues.discovery: Medical comparison of the two injuries; another healer can reach the same broad conclusion.

clues.title: The tested bottle excludes Mara's kitchen as the murder method
clues.description: The sealed bottle, remaining volume, and recipe establish one nonlethal dose from Perrin's stock. Mara controlled Merrit's supper service and concealed brandy, but neither the wine nor the measured medicine explains the focused head wound.
clues.discovery: Test the bottle and compare the result with the wound before treating kitchen access as a poisoning method.

clues.title: The gauge slate fixes rain at 8:50
clues.description: Senn’s contemporaneous slate records the 8:45 shaft chime, the abrupt gauge rise at 8:50, and the immediate emergency stop. Rain therefore began ten minutes before the last bell.
clues.discovery: Automatic from the slate, gauge marks, and still-hot brake; no witness’s later estimate stands alone.

clues.title: Cora’s sealed notice explains the flour and scrape
clues.description: Cora’s retained copy and cord match the flour and shallow wrist scrape from her 5:40 attempt to recover an ergot notice from Merrit.
clues.discovery: Found beneath the account stone or produced when Cora is confronted with the matching sample.

clues.title: The emergency stop accounts for Cora during the killing
clues.description: The hot brake, capstan hand marks, displaced grain, and Senn’s diagram place Cora at the wheel from before the rain through the last bell.
clues.discovery: Physical reconstruction plus Senn’s account; neither alone is treated as conclusive.

clues.title: Mill carts carried Hester’s bridge stone
clues.description: The cart ledger and surviving quarry marks account for three disputed loads at the east bridge, showing where Hester’s unauthorized money went.
clues.discovery: Compare haul entries with Hester’s voucher numbers and the stone already set in the pier.

clues.title: Ghost-hearth grain went to school carriers
clues.description: Six years of grain entries cite Common Chest warrant numbers for Dolly Reed, Milo Tansy, and Pipkin Wold; originals were surrendered after redemption.
clues.discovery: Automatic from the redemption book once the three names or warrant sequence is known.

clues.title: School helpers collected the fictitious hearth shares
clues.description: Rotating pupil and kitchen-helper marks show the ghost-hearth grain was carried to Bramblewick School under Orlo’s standing instruction.
clues.discovery: Compare carrier marks across years; Cora identifies the regular school collection practice.

clues.title: The sluice lane joins the North Hedge
clues.description: A service lane used by grain carriers meets the low hedge gate and school wash yard, allowing the route and its rain-softened traces to be inspected from the mill side.
clues.discovery: Automatic exterior survey or Cora’s directions.

clues.title: The mill chronology leaves Orlo’s crossing interval
clues.description: The 8:50 rain mark, blood already exposed to rain, and Orlo’s school arrival around 8:54 leave time for the pre-rain hall-to-school crossing but not his claimed continuous rehearsal.
clues.discovery: Inference after comparing the mill slate with the preserved blood sequence and school timeline.

clues.title: The first warrants retain the children’s memorial marks
clues.description: The earliest warrants preserve tiny memorial crosses beside Dolly Reed, Milo Tansy, and Pipkin Wold, while Merrit’s annotations pair each with a childhood burial date.
clues.discovery: Compare the oldest warrant bundle with Merrit’s copied audit table.

clues.title: Six years of shares end in school redemptions
clues.description: Grain, meals, shoes, cloaks, slate, lamp oil, and soap drawn by the three nonexistent hearths all return with the school seal or Orlo’s receiving initials.
clues.discovery: Build at least three complete warrant chains across different years and goods.

clues.title: Orlo wrote the authorizations and receiving marks
clues.description: The ghost-hearth authorizations and school receipts share Orlo’s clean-copy hand, showing his direct control of the records rather than merely benefiting from Merrit’s bookkeeping.
clues.discovery: Ordinary side-by-side comparison; scribal expertise formalizes the handwriting features.

clues.title: Hester’s unlawful spending is physically accounted for
clues.description: Quarry tallies, mason receipts, mill-cart marks, and stone in the east pier account for the entire disputed bridge sum.
clues.discovery: Sort the bridge file separately from the ghost-hearth warrants and verify one external record.

clues.title: The warrant bundle points back to the chapel register
clues.description: Merrit’s slips beside the three household files cite the Open Door burial pages needed to prove the names never became adult hearths.
clues.discovery: Automatic when the ghost-hearth bundle is opened.

clues.title: The receiving seal and beneficiary numbers lead to the school
clues.description: School seals, supply categories, and a sealed family-initial packet identify Bramblewick School as the distribution center and Orlo as its custodian.
clues.discovery: Automatic from the surrendered originals; beneficiary names need not be opened.

clues.title: Grain warrant originals were redeemed at Bramble Mill
clues.description: Mill stamps on the ghost-hearth grain warrants identify dates and sack numbers that Cora’s redemption book can check independently.
clues.discovery: Found in the grain subset of the six-year bundles.

clues.title: Nim can certify a narrow warrant chain
clues.description: Nim offers to seal three representative warrant chains for presentation at the First-Bell Moot, avoiding an unreadable cartload of records.
clues.discovery: Available after the party preserves custody and identifies representative examples.

clues.title: Only Orlo owns the threatened scheme
clues.description: Merrit threatened exposure of a six-year scheme created in Orlo’s hand, controlled through his seal, and defended for his beneficiaries; none of the other suspects is tied to the ghost warrants.
clues.discovery: Inference from the clean-copy authorizations, receiving chain, and Merrit’s audit threat.

clues.title: The chest supplies a complete motive exhibit
clues.description: A certified authorization-to-redemption chain establishes the ghost-hearth scheme, Orlo’s control, and Merrit’s reason to confront him without naming every beneficiary.
clues.discovery: Established when the party selects and seals at least one complete example from the six-year series.

clues.title: All three names belong to children who died young
clues.description: The burial register records Dolly Reed at six, Milo Tansy at nine, and Pipkin Wold at four; none could later establish the adult hearth appearing in the current book.
clues.discovery: Automatic from Amity’s supervised reading of the named entries.

clues.title: Orlo borrowed the register before the false hearths appeared
clues.description: A signed lending slip and red guide marks show Orlo selected the three entries while preparing a school memorial roll one month before the first ghost warrants.
clues.discovery: Compare the lending slip, marked pages, and dated memorial program.

clues.title: Merrit’s correction slips point back to his private folios
clues.description: Each annual notice carries Merrit's tiny 'home copy' mark and a bundle reference. Sister Amity says the corresponding working folios were returned to his burrow after certification.
clues.discovery: Inspect the yearly notice copies and ask where Merrit kept the working set.

clues.title: Merrit’s certified copy cites the Common Chest series
clues.description: A copy Merrit left with Amity pairs each burial entry with the first disputed warrant number, directing investigators to the Common Chest chain.
clues.discovery: Produced when Amity understands the inquiry concerns adult shares rather than the deaths themselves.

clues.title: Orlo’s memorial program links the selected names to school work
clues.description: The school memorial program groups the three children in Orlo’s clean hand and predates the fictitious hearths by one month.
clues.discovery: Found in the chapel’s Founders’ programs or recalled by Amity.

clues.title: Amity will certify the names without exposing beneficiaries
clues.description: Amity offers sealed copies of the three entries and the lending slip for the First-Bell Moot, while keeping family grief and beneficiary identities separate.
clues.discovery: Available once the party states the limited propositions it intends to prove.

clues.title: Orlo selected the names Merrit was about to expose
clues.description: The lending slip, guide marks, and memorial program tie Orlo personally to the names at the center of Merrit’s announced audit, giving him a motive no innocent suspect shares.
clues.discovery: Inference after comparing the chapel dates with Merrit’s audit and the first warrants.

clues.title: The pupils completed four stanzas before Orlo arrived
clues.description: Tella’s count marks, Nibs’s rain sketch, and the practice candle place Orlo’s first correction in the final stanza, shortly before the last bell.
clues.discovery: Reconstruct the rehearsal from physical records before asking the children to agree on exact minutes.

clues.title: Jory saw Orlo enter at 8:54
clues.description: Jory Pike saw Orlo enter through the school side door while crossing to ring the bell, confirming a late arrival rather than a brief absence during continuous leadership.
clues.discovery: Interview Jory separately; the revelation remains supported without him.

clues.title: The missing blue chalk stick matches the clock wedge
clues.description: The surviving half of a missing school chalk stick fits the clock wedge by fracture face and paper dust, showing the pendulum was stopped with school material.
clues.discovery: Compare the wrapped chalk packet with the preserved wedge; it identifies supply, not unique possession by itself.

clues.title: Orlo’s copyist key carries map-room lime
clues.description: The authorized hall key on Orlo’s ring bears fresh pale lime in its ward, and his copyist tools match the clean Hearth Book entries.
clues.discovery: Inventory the key ring with witnesses and compare the deposit to the map-room jamb.

clues.title: The beneficiary box is indexed by ghost-hearth warrants
clues.description: Meal chits, shoe measures, and relief payments in Orlo’s cedar box cite the same three warrant series used by the nonexistent hearths.
clues.discovery: Open the box under custody; family names may remain sealed while numbers and categories are copied.

clues.title: The wash basin holds blood dilution and Merrit’s collar lint
clues.description: Reddish dilution, green wool matching Merrit’s collar, and lavender soap on Orlo’s freshly washed right cuff place him cleaning after the hall-to-school crossing.
clues.discovery: Inspect the basin, drain splinter, and coat together; none of the traces is treated as a unique laboratory identifier.

clues.title: Orlo revises both his presence and his entrance
clues.description: Orlo changes continuous presence into continuous responsibility, then changes a front-door arrival into chapel work after the side-door evidence appears. The revisions align with the physical route rather than an innocent errand.
clues.discovery: Record his first account before revealing the practice sheets, then compare later answers.

clues.title: The side yard opens directly onto the North Hedge
clues.description: The covered wash yard and grated drain meet the hedge path hidden from the green, making it the route to test against Orlo’s late arrival.
clues.discovery: Automatic exterior inspection.

clues.title: The school box preserves Common Chest warrant numbers
clues.description: Distribution chits repeat the Common Chest numbers and dates needed to trace the school supplies back to fictitious household shares.
clues.discovery: Compare the cedar-box index with any school receipt or Merrit’s audit.

clues.title: The selected names came from an Open Door memorial roll
clues.description: Orlo’s old school memorial copy groups Dolly, Milo, and Pipkin and notes the Open Door register as its source.
clues.discovery: Found among clean-copy exemplars in the school cabinet.

clues.title: Three school exhibits carry the case
clues.description: Tella proposes carrying only the practice sheets, key inventory, and sealed warrant index to the moot, allowing the party to present the case without parading the beneficiary box.
clues.discovery: Available after the children understand which records answer which claim.

clues.title: The school gathers the broken alibi, the chalk, and the fund
clues.description: The interrupted rehearsal, matching chalk, authorized key, school-fund records, and wash-yard traces form independent strands that can be presented together without relying on confession.
clues.discovery: Inference after at least three of the school evidence groups have been preserved.

clues.title: Fresh school ash matches the missing audit leaves
clues.description: Rag-paper ash, red ruling pigment, and binding-thread fragments behind the rear stove door match Merrit's torn audit folio. No writing survives, but the fresh burn carries the missing comparison leaves to the school immediately before Orlo's 8:54 arrival.
clues.discovery: Inspect the rear ash door before the stove is fed again and compare the ash, pigment, and thread with the torn folio.

clues.title: A direct track crossed before the rain
clues.description: Shallow impressions rounded by later rain run from the map-room lane to the school, beneath sharper tracks made after the ground was wet.
clues.discovery: Sequence inspection under the hedge overhang; tracking skill adds detail but is not required.

clues.title: The garden door can be pulled closed but not latched
clues.description: A reconstruction from outside reproduces the recorded closed-but-unlatched door, confirming an exit through the garden after lawful entry.
clues.discovery: Demonstrate with the ordinary outer strap while preserving the latch position.

clues.title: Lime beneath mud and a blue cuff thread mark the crossing
clues.description: Map-room lime lies beneath rain mud in the old track, and dark blue wool matching Orlo’s coat catches on the schoolward side of the gate.
clues.discovery: Lift and record both traces before reopening the path.

clues.title: The dry route fits an 8:48 departure and 8:54 arrival
clues.description: A five-to-six-minute dry-ground walk connects the murder scene to Orlo’s late fourth-stanza arrival; current wet-ground timing would misleadingly add several minutes.
clues.discovery: Timed reconstruction corrected for the observed dry pre-rain surface.

clues.title: The old track ends at the school wash yard
clues.description: The direct pre-rain impressions terminate beside the covered basin and side door rather than continuing to the green.
clues.discovery: Follow the sequence to its schoolward end.

clues.title: The orchard work site overlooks but does not join the direct track
clues.description: The lower orchard gate reveals Bram’s separate tether and work circle above the route, allowing his storm work to be checked without treating every nearby print as his.
clues.discovery: Survey the gate and sightline with Bram’s claimed work site in view.

clues.title: The sluice lane ties the track sequence to the mill’s rain mark
clues.description: The adjacent delivery lane reaches the mill gauge, whose 8:50 jump determines whether the rounded impressions predate the storm.
clues.discovery: Cora’s lane markers or a direct walk identify the independent timing source.

clues.title: Only Orlo fits the whole crossing
clues.description: The unforced hall entry, old schoolward track, matching blue thread, lime, washed cuff, and 8:54 arrival converge on Orlo’s movement after the killing.
clues.discovery: Inference after comparing the hedge evidence with the hall key list and school timeline.

clues.title: The route can be proved without naming a footprint
clues.description: Measured distance, the door-strap demonstration, mill rain mark, rounded track, and school arrival provide a defensible movement reconstruction for the moot.
clues.discovery: Established when the party records the sequence and selects corroborating exhibits.

clues.title: The hedge traces separate Bram from the killer's crossing
clues.description: Bram's green-brown cuff damage and work circle remain above the lower gate; the direct pre-rain crossing carries a dark blue thread and map-room lime toward the school. His earlier map-room traces do not continue along the killer's route.
clues.discovery: Compare the orchard work site, Bram's torn cuff, and the direct hedge track rather than assigning every nearby trace to one visit.

clues.title: The public clock demonstration survives challenge
clues.description: Separated shards, the chalk wedge, and the clock's recent service record let the party demonstrate that the display was constructed after blood had spread rather than stopped by the killing.
clues.discovery: Present the preserved clock evidence in any order; no confession or clockmaker is required.

clues.title: Separated rehearsal evidence fixes Orlo’s late arrival
clues.description: The marked practice sheets, candle band, rain notation, and separately heard witnesses agree that four stanzas passed before Orlo made his first correction.
clues.discovery: Call any two corroborating witnesses or present the physical rehearsal records; Jory Pike remains optional.

clues.title: The door and route can be reconstructed before the village
clues.description: The outer strap closes the garden door without latching it, while the measured dry route, pre-rain track, and mill rain mark carry the killer from Hearth Hall to the school side.
clues.discovery: Perform the strap demonstration and lay the route measurements beside the recorded track sequence.

clues.title: A narrow certified chain proves the school diversion
clues.description: One sealed sequence of authorization, redemption, school receipt, and beneficiary index proves the flow of shares without naming every supported family.
clues.discovery: Have Nim Thatch and Sister Amity certify the representative records under seal.

clues.title: Orlo concedes every instrument while denying the sequence
clues.description: Under narrow questioning, Orlo admits the copyist key, blue chalk, school warrants, register loan, hedge familiarity, and recent washing, leaving only the claim that these facts never formed one act.
clues.discovery: Ask about each independently preserved item before presenting the full reconstruction.

clues.title: The whole sequence leaves no innocent substitute
clues.description: Early death, staged clock, lawful key, pre-rain route, late school arrival, wash-yard traces, and the threatened fund converge on Orlo; each innocent suspect's secret explains only earlier or separate evidence.
clues.discovery: Established when the party presents the sequence and answers the strongest remaining alternative theory; confession is unnecessary.

clues.title: Perrin's dose and sickroom sequence survive public testing
clues.description: The measured bottle, the Fen household's timed cooling work, and the focused wound can be examined as separate exhibits. Together they expose Perrin's record alteration while excluding both his medicine and his movements as the murder method.
clues.discovery: Available if Perrin remains accused and the party calls the bottle custodian, a Fen witness, and a healer or wound record before the moot.
